result.anchor_violation_rationale: No claims were supported or rejected using held-out anchor AR-BLOTEVOGEL-2023; assessments relied solely on the provided verified records and excerpts.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Batch PFOS SCWO reaches 70% PFOS conversion at 500 °C, 60 min; defluorination is 78.2% under the same condition, with total F recovery >75% only at ≥475 °C.
claim_assessments.rationale: S02 reports maximum PFOS destruction efficiency of 70.0% and maximum fluorine conversion (defluorination) of 78.2% at 500 °C, 60 min (S02-E01,E04). S02-E04 states total fluorine mass balance >75% at 475 and 500 °C. The claim matches these values and conditions.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Continuous-flow SCWO mixture studies report DRE >99.999% for PFOS/PFOA/PFHpS at 650 °C, ~30 s.
claim_assessments.rationale: S04-E08 states that 99.999% destruction of PFOS, PFHpS, and PFOA and complete defluorination were observed at 650 °C and ~30 s residence time. This matches the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Continuous-flow SCWO mixture studies report DRE >99.999% ... for a 12‑PFAA AFFF suite at field scale.
claim_assessments.rationale: S09-E06 reports greater than 99.999% destruction and removal efficiency for the sum of 12 PFAAs after two continuous-flow field-scale SCWO trials. Temperature is ~650 °C from context; although not restated in S09 chunks, high T is consistent and DRE >99.999% for 12 PFAAs is explicitly supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Pilot systems treating diluted AFFF (Aquarden, Battelle, 374Water) show >99.99% PFOS removal and large PFOA reductions.
claim_assessments.rationale: For Battelle, S17-E03 shows PFOS reduced from ~30,600–30,300 µg/L to 0.33–0.29 µg/L (>99.99% reduction). For Aquarden and 374Water, S17-E01 shows strong PFOS decreases (to 0.310 µg/L and 8.57 µg/L) but does not give explicit initial PFOS for Aquarden, so % removal >99.99% is not directly documented for all three systems. PFOA reductions are clearly large for all three (S17-E01). Thus the direction is supported but the universal >99.99% qualifier is only partly traceable.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Bench-scale AFFF HALT at 350 °C, ≥2 h and 5 M NaOH yields >99% reduction in total detected PFAS across 40 analytes, with no new targeted PFAS observed.
claim_assessments.rationale: S13-E08 describes HALT at 350 °C, >20.7 MPa, 5 M NaOH, 2–6 h. S13-E07 states all tests reduce total PFAS levels by >99% and that only PFAS present in initial AFFF are detected post-treatment, even at lower MDLs. This supports both the >99% reduction and lack of new target analytes.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Pilot HALT on industrial wastewater reports %Degradation based on targeted PFAS concentration loss, but does not publish numeric values in the excerpts.
claim_assessments.rationale: S05-E03 defines %Degradation based on C0 and C for target PFAS measured by LC‑MS/MS. The provided S05 excerpts do not contain specific %Degradation results, consistent with the statement.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Reverse-vortex gliding arc plasma (GAP) gives 21% PFOA loss at 20 min, 150 W (in the “most energy-efficient” regime discussed).
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E08 reports that the most energy efficient removal was 21% destruction and 17% defluorination in 20 minutes at 150 W. This matches the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Hydrodynamic cavitation (HC) of PFOS shows gradual parent loss; degradation per pass peaks at ~1.6% and totals ~20% defluorination by the end of the experiment.
claim_assessments.rationale: S06-E06 states maximum degradation per pass of ~1.6% and maximum defluorination per pass of ~0.44%. S06-E02 reports defluorination reaching ~20% by the end at 5 mg/L PFOS. Together these support the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Bench ultrasonication of PFOA, PFOS and 6:2 FTS routinely achieves >80–100% parent loss in MQ, CW and SW.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E08 reports degradation efficiencies for PFOA, PFOS, and 6:2 FTS of 96–98% in SW, 81–100% in MQ, and 67–99% in CW, with PFOA completely removed in MQ and CW. This supports the stated >80–100% range in MQ and CW; for CW, some 6:2 FTS removal is 67%, slightly below 80%, so the claim is directionally correct but slightly overstates the lower bound. Overall judged supported given ranges.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In real groundwater, total measured PFAS drop from ~111 ppb to 16.6 ppb (~85% removal) but PFHxS and PFOS remain.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E03 states PFAS in GW were reduced from ~111 ppb to 16.6 ppb, an 85% removal, with remaining PFAS comprising PFHxS (~2.5 ppb) and PFOS (~14.1 ppb).

claim_assessments.claim_text: Batch proof-of-concept EC treatment in deionized/distilled water (DDW) yields 95–98% PFOA/PFOS “removal” in 1 h, but with no F⁻ detected.
claim_assessments.rationale: S10-E04 reports removal efficiencies of 95.3±0.7% for PFOA and 98±3% for PFOS after 1 h in DDW, and explicitly states that in the PFAS systems fluorides were not observed. DDW matrix is given in S10-E04/E03.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Continuous EC for PFAS mixtures in tap water reduces most PFAS by 1–2 orders of magnitude at 80 min, with PFBA largely persisting.
claim_assessments.rationale: S10-E07 tabulates initial and steady-state concentrations at 30 and 80 min, showing large reductions (roughly 1–2 orders of magnitude) for PFOS, PFOA, PFDA, PFNA but PFBA decreases only slightly (16.6→13.2→13.8 µg/L). This supports the qualitative pattern. The specific matrix 'tap water' is not explicitly stated in S10-E07 (the water type is only 'aqueous PFAS mixture'), so that qualifier is inferred.

claim_assessments.claim_text: BN-assisted ball milling of undiluted AFFF reports disappearance of 6:2/8:2 FTS, PFHxA, PFOA and other n = 6–7 precursors within 6 h.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E01 reports that milling 0.5 g BN with 100 µL AFFF led to destruction of 6:2 FTS, 8:2 FTS, and precursors, with PFHxA and PFOA as intermediates, and that 'targeted PFAS and precursors were destroyed after 6 h of reaction.' The AFFF is treated undiluted (matrix from S01-R01).

claim_assessments.claim_text: Quartz-sand MCD of AFFF and contaminated soil achieves 99.88–100% loss of targeted PFAS subgroups, including PFHxS and PFOS.
claim_assessments.rationale: S08-E04 states that destruction efficiencies of target PFAS subgroups ranged from 99.88% to 100%. S08-E01 notes PFHxS and PFOS reached 100% DE by 120 min milling in AFFF. Soil data also show near-complete destruction (S08-E05,E07).

claim_assessments.claim_text: For PFOA in DI water, 93% parent loss in 120 min; for PFOS, 88%.
claim_assessments.rationale: For PFOA, S15-E06 reports 93% degradation after 120 min. For PFOS, S15-E06 reports 88% degradation after 120 min. DI water matrix is confirmed in S15-E06/E08.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Across technologies, parent loss alone consistently overstates the degree of PFAS destruction because shorter-chain PFAS or other TPs often rise as parents drop.
claim_assessments.rationale: Multiple sources support this pattern: S04-E06/E08 show PFOS yielding PFCAs and VOFs at intermediate T/T; S11-E05/E08 show short-chain PFCAs/PFHpS rising as PFOA/PFOS/6:2 FTS degrade; S17-E03 shows PFDA, PFTrDA, 6:2 FTS present/increasing in SCWO effluent; S14-E02/E06 show formation of PFOA from PFOS and PFOS from 8:2 FtS and chain-shortened PFCAs; S08-E01/E05 show transient PFCAs and PFOS as intermediates; S15-E01/E06 indicate short-chain products and low TOC removal. Collectively they support the conceptual claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: PFOS yields a suite of PFCAs (PFOA, PFHxA, PFPeA, PFBA, PFPrA, TFA) at 420–600 °C, with TFA persisting even at 600 °C, 32 s; volatile organofluorines including 1H‑perfluorohexane are detected in gas-phase products.
claim_assessments.rationale: S04-E06 and E08 report that at 420–600 °C PFOS experiments yielded PFCAs (PFOA, PFHxA, PFPeA, PFBA, PFPrA, TFA) and that TFA was the most recalcitrant intermediate, persisting at 600 °C and ~32 s. S04-E06 mentions gas-phase analysis revealing VOF such as 1H‑perfluoroalkane/perfluorohexane.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Battelle continuous SCWO: PFDA increases in effluent; PFTrDA and 6:2 FTS are below MDL in influent but above MDL in effluent.
claim_assessments.rationale: S17-E03 states PFDA concentration increased in the effluent of the second Battelle test and that PFTrDA and 6:2 FTS were below MDL in influents and above MDL in effluent.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Continuous-flow SCWO on PFAS mixtures at 510 °C: all PFCAs go below MDL, but PFOS/PFHpS remain; PFHxS appears in effluent even though it was below MDL in stock, implying low-level presence rather than in‑reactor formation.
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E03 describes that at 510 °C all PFCAs were below MDL while PFOS and PFHpS had DRE <40%. S03-E08 notes PFHxS was not detected in stock but detected at 11 µg/L in treated effluent at 510 °C and interprets this as PFHxS being present below MDL in untreated stock, not formed in reactor.

claim_assessments.claim_text: PFOA, PFOS and 6:2 FTS degrade to PFPeA, PFHxA, PFHpA, PFHpS in various water matrices under ultrasonication.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E05 states that PFOA degraded to traces of PFPeA, PFHxA, PFHpA; 6:2 FTS intermediates included PFHxA and PFHpA (and small PFPeA in CW); PFOS degraded to PFHpS (and trace PFHpA/PFHxA depending on matrix).

claim_assessments.claim_text: TOP assay and targeted panels for AFFF/foam fractionate and contaminated groundwater show decrease of parent PFAS with likely formation of ultrashort PFCAs (TFA, PFPrA) that are not well captured by standard methods.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E01/E11-E02/E11-E03 discuss use of TOP assay with AFFF/FF/GW and emphasize analytical difficulty in detecting ultrashort PFAS like TFA and PFPrA; they state such products may be overlooked, leading to underestimation of degradation/mineralisation. However, 'likely formation' of ultrashort PFCAs in these specific runs is an inference; the text highlights expectation and detection challenges rather than direct observation. Thus the caution about poor capture is supported, but the assertion of likely formation in these experiments is only partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Cross-formation of PFOA from PFOS and PFOS from 8:2 FTS confirms headgroup cleavage and telomer degradation in plasma GAP.
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E02 explicitly notes formation of PFOA during treatment of PFOS and formation of PFOS during treatment of 8:2 FtS, indicating headgroup cleavage and transformation among PFAS species.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In AFFF and impacted soil, C6–C9 PFCAs (PFHxA, PFPeA, PFBA) rise and fall over milling time, clearly acting as intermediates from fluorotelomers and other precursors.
claim_assessments.rationale: For AFFF, S08-E01 describes PFHxA, PFPeA, PFBA increasing after 480 min, reaching a max at 720 min, then degrading, and interprets them as intermediate products from degradation of target and non-target PFAS such as 6:2 FTS. For soil, S08-E05 mentions similar patterns for C6–C9 PFCAs acting as intermediates. This supports the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: PFOS itself behaves as a transient intermediate in soil (formation then disappearance) under mechanochemical treatment.
claim_assessments.rationale: S08-E01 notes that PFOS showed 'formation and degradation kinetic progression, suggesting that PFOS was an intermediate product of other non-target precursor PFASs' in the AFFF system; for soil, S08-E05 notes PFOSA as precursor. While soil-specific PFOS kinetics are not detailed in the provided soil chunks, the AFFF evidence clearly supports PFOS acting as an intermediate. Soil extension is somewhat inferred but consistent; overall judged supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: The PFOA photocatalysis study infers short-chain PFCAs and partially oxidized intermediates from ATR‑FTIR and mass balance; direct LC‑MS TP identification was not completed.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E01 describes ATR‑FTIR evidence of short-chain carboxylates and decreased C–F bands; S15-E06 states 'Although direct identification of intermediates by LC-MS was not performed...' and infers intermediates from TOC and mass balance. This matches the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: For PFOS under CS@g‑C3N4 photocatalysis, short-chain fluorinated products are also inferred rather than comprehensively quantified.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E01/E15-E06/E15-E08 discuss mechanistic inference of partially oxidized fluorinated intermediates and short-chain products for both PFOA and PFOS; explicit quantitative TP lists are not provided for PFOS in the excerpts. The inference part is supported; 'short-chain fluorinated products' for PFOS specifically are not directly enumerated, so the scope is partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: High-resolution suspect/non‑target screening during EO of landfill leachate and groundwater reveals numerous novel PFAS classes (e.g., FASHN, MeOH‑FASA, H‑PFSA, PFPrES, multiple sulfonamide/sulfonate-related PFAS) plus chlorinated/brominated byproducts.
claim_assessments.rationale: S16-E04 and S16-E08 list new PFAS classes such as FASHN and MeOH‑FASA and several other PFAS-related transformation products, and note formation of six chlorinated or brominated compounds. This directly supports the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: BN–ball milling of undiluted AFFF achieves 99.7% defluorination for 100 µL in 6 h and >98% for 200 µL in 8 h; DeF is based on IC‑measured F⁻ and TOF₀ from CIC/IC.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E01 reports 99.7% defluorination of undiluted AFFF after 6 h BN‑BM for 100 µL. S01-E08 states >98% defluorination after 8 h for 200 µL. S01-E02/E03 explain DeF calculation based on F⁻ (IC) and [TOF]₀ from CIC/IC. All elements are supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: HALT single 2 h run on 10× AFFF gives measured F⁻ equal to 120.5% of theoretical fluorine from 40 quantified PFAS, with authors noting that theoretical fluorine underestimates actual fluorine due to unmeasured PFAS.
claim_assessments.rationale: S13-E04 reports that measured fluoride after 2 h HALT is 120.5% of theoretical fluorine based on measured PFAS (~21,887 mg/L) and that this theoretical value likely underestimates total fluorine due to PFAS below MDL and PFAS outside the 40-analyte list.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Batch PFOS SCWO achieves defluorination of 78.2% and total fluorine mass balance >75% at high temperatures (475–500 °C).
claim_assessments.rationale: S02-E01/E04 state maximum defluorination of 78.2% at 500 °C, 60 min; S02-E04 notes fluorine mass balance >75% at 475 and 500 °C.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Continuous PFOS/PFOA/PFHpS SCWO mixture at 650 °C, 30 s reports complete defluorination with DRE >99.999%.
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E03 concludes that at 650 °C, DRE >99.999% and complete defluorination were achieved after 30 s exposure. The PFAS mixture is PFSAs and PFCAs (S03-E07).

claim_assessments.claim_text: Field-scale SCWO on 12 PFAAs from AFFF waste shows average overall defluorination ratio ~62.6%, with ~28.1% of theoretical fluorine unrecovered in measured fluoride.
claim_assessments.rationale: S09-E06 reports overall defluorination of approximately 62.6%. S09-E02 indicates that 28.1% (152.9 mmol) of anticipated molar fluorine was not recovered in the fluoride balance.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Hydrodynamic cavitation of PFOS reaches ~20% defluorination at 5 mg/L PFOS, with fluorine mass balance 97–104% across time.
claim_assessments.rationale: S06-E02 reports defluorination reaching approximately 20% by the end for [PFOS]₀=5 mg/L. S06-E05 notes fluorine mass balance within 97–104% over the whole treatment time.

claim_assessments.claim_text: GAP plasma for PFOA achieves 17% defluorination versus 21% parent loss in the 20 min, 150 W experiment; longer runs increase F⁻ but defluorination still lags destruction.
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E08 gives 21% destruction and 17% defluorination at 20 min, 150 W. S14-E05 states that destruction over time is greatly reduced while defluorination occurs at a much slower pace, indicating lagging defluorination with longer treatment.

claim_assessments.claim_text: For PFOA photocatalysis in DI water, aqueous F⁻ is only 0.0256 mg of 2.568 mg input (~1% of fluorine) after 120 min; total recovered fluorine is 2.35% of initial across all measured pools.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E06 states starting fluorine 2.568 mg, aqueous fluoride 0.0256 mg, and total fluorine recovery across all pools 2.35% after 120 min. 0.0256/2.568≈1%, consistent with the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: PFOS under the same photocatalyst shows 88% parent loss, 23% TOC removal, and reduced fluoride formation in natural matrices.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E06 reports 88% PFOS degradation and 23% TOC removal after 120 min. S15-E08 notes that in natural matrices the amount of liberated fluoride decreases relative to DI water, consistent with 'reduced fluoride formation'.

claim_assessments.claim_text: For 10 ppm PFOA under ultrasonication, defluorination reaches 56–86% depending on matrix and salt, while parent loss is higher (often 100%), and PFOS and 6:2 FTS show the same 'removal > defluorination' relationship.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E08 indicates defluorination of 10 ppm PFOA of 86% (MQ), 56% (SW), 85% (CW) without salt and shows PFOA removal up to 100% in MQ and CW. S11-E05 and E08 note that degradation percentages for PFOA, PFOS, 6:2 FTS are high while defluorination is lower, due to fluorinated intermediates. This matches the described pattern.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Real GW ultrasonication shows 85% parent loss and lower, unspecific defluorination; mass balance cannot be closed.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E03 gives ~85% PFAS removal (111→16.6 ppb) in GW. The excerpts emphasize difficulties in achieving mass balance and under-detection of ultrashort PFAS, but they do not provide explicit defluorination percentages for GW or state that mass balance 'cannot be closed' for this specific case, though this is consistent with their stated limitations. Thus the qualitative part about incomplete mass balance is supported; the precise 'cannot be closed' phrasing is inferential.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Aquarden SCWO: fluoride increases from 26.0 mg/L to 97.5 mg/L, while fluorine in 28 targeted PFAS drops from 2.78 mg/L to 0.006 mg/L; stoichiometric expectation based on targeted PFAS is 25.9 mg/L F⁻, so detected PFAS account for only 27% of F⁻.
claim_assessments.rationale: S17-E06 reports influent fluoride 26.0 mg/L, effluent 97.5 mg/L, influent fluorine in 28 PFAS 2.78 mg/L, effluent 0.006 mg/L. S17-E02 states only 25.9 mg F/L fluoride would be expected from detected PFAS, accounting for 27% of measured 97.5 mg/L. All figures match.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Electrochemical treatment in DDW removes >95% PFOA and PFOS in 1 h but no fluoride is observed, indicating physical removal/electrocoagulation rather than destruction.
claim_assessments.rationale: S10-E04 reports 95.3% PFOA and 98% PFOS removal after 1 h in DDW with no fluoride observed for PFAS systems; S10-E08 discusses chemically inert PFAS being removed via electrocoagulation rather than chemical degradation. The inference that lack of fluoride implies physical removal is consistent with authors' interpretation.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In the ultrasonic field demonstration, F⁻ rises as PFAS and AOF decrease, but the F⁻ increase is substantially smaller than the AOF decrease; authors note that organic fluorine mineralized to F⁻ did not equate to the total decrease in moles of AOF.
claim_assessments.rationale: S07-E06 states that fluoride generally increased as PFAS decreased but that '[SOURCE_TEXT_OMITTED sha256=0d67b7ca4039bbef8357a1d27e1632bda5f692535d4f694a05728af79465f0ef]', exactly matching the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: HALT 2 h AFFF bench test: theoretical fluorine from 40 PFAS analytes ~21,887 mg/L; measured fluoride = 120.5% of that value, indicating near-complete defluorination of measured and some unmeasured PFAS.
claim_assessments.rationale: S13-E04 reports theoretical total fluorine ~21,887 mg/L based on measured PFAS, with measured fluoride at 120.5% of that value, and notes that theoretical F underestimates true F, implying additional PFAS were also defluorinated.

claim_assessments.claim_text: For 5 mg/L PFOS under hydrodynamic cavitation, total fluorine mass balance ([F⁻]+PFOS‑bound F) stays within 97–104% of initial throughout the run; shorter-chain PFCAs are not detected above 0.05 mol%.
claim_assessments.rationale: S06-E05 states fluoride mass balance within 97–104% over treatment time, with total fluorine assessed as F⁻ plus PFOS-bound F. S06-E08 notes no shorter-chain perfluorocarboxylates detected in aqueous phase above 0.05 mol% of initial PFOS.

claim_assessments.claim_text: For PFOA photocatalysis, fluorine balance accounts for only 2.35% of theoretical fluorine across aqueous F⁻, residual PFOA, identified TPs and adsorbed F.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E06 explicitly states that only 2.35% of initial fluorine is recovered across aqueous fluoride, residual PFOA, TPs and catalyst-adsorbed fluorine after 120 min.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Field-scale SCWO (McDonough) shows average defluorination ~62.6%, with ~28.1% of fluorine unrecovered.
claim_assessments.rationale: S09-E06 gives overall defluorination 62.6%. S09-E02 states that on average 28.1% (152.9 mmol) of anticipated fluorine was not recovered.

claim_assessments.claim_text: The FSE method paper stresses that increased F⁻ is a strong but non‑exclusive indicator of PFAS degradation; multiple transformation pathways and incomplete PFAS characterization mean that F⁻ cannot be equated with complete mineralization.
claim_assessments.rationale: S12-E02 states that while increases in aqueous fluoride are suggestive of PFAS degradation, they should not be considered to represent complete mineralization due to multiple transformation pathways and incomplete PFAS characterization. This matches the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Photocatalysis: TOC removal is 27.1% for PFOA (vs 93% parent loss) and 23% for PFOS (vs 88% parent loss) after 120 min, showing most PFAS carbon remains organic.
claim_assessments.rationale: S15-E06 reports 93% PFOA degradation with 27.1% TOC removal and 88% PFOS degradation with 23% TOC removal after 120 min. The interpretation that most carbon remains in organic form is consistent with these numbers.

claim_assessments.claim_text: BN‑ball milling of AFFF leaves ~50% of TOC remaining after treatment, indicating near‑complete defluorination does not equate to carbon mineralization.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E07 states that approximately 50% of the TOC of AFFF remained after BN‑BM treatment, while S01-E01/E02 report near-complete defluorination (≈99.7%). This supports the conclusion that carbon is not fully mineralized.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Several SCWO and HALT papers use 'mineralize' conceptually but do not report CO₂ or inorganic carbon data in the provided text; strongest support is high PFAS DRE, substantial fluorine release, and, in some cases, COD reduction (e.g., 4,750 to 5.17 mg/L in Aquarden’s effluent).
claim_assessments.rationale: The provided excerpts from S02–S04, S09, S13, S17 report high DRE, significant defluorination, and COD reductions (e.g., S17-E06, COD 4,750→5.17 mg/L). They do not mention CO₂ or full carbon balance measurements. However, the assertion that these papers explicitly use the term 'mineralize' in the excerpts is not uniformly documented here; some usage is contextual. Thus, the description of endpoints is supported, while the generalization about language is only partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In hydrodynamic cavitation and GAP studies, high fluoride yield per degraded PFOS/PFOA and absence of shorter-chain intermediates above low detection limits are interpreted as 'near-complete mineralization' of the fraction that enters reaction zones, but no CO₂ or carbon balances are measured.
claim_assessments.rationale: S06-E08/E06 interpret high fluoride yields and absence of shorter-chain PFCAs as evidence of near-complete mineralization of PFOS reaching the cavitation bubble, while noting the study cannot definitively prove the mechanism. S14-E05/E08 emphasize defluorination and chain shortening in GAP; the specific phrase 'near-complete mineralization' is used in S14-E08 for PFOA fraction. None of the cited excerpts report CO₂ or full carbon balances. The interpretive language is author-reported, but the extrapolation to 'no carbon balance' across both studies is based on absence of evidence in the excerpts, so classification is partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In the ultrasonic field study, authors frame high-frequency ultrasound as 'mineralizing' PFAS to F⁻ and CO₂ based on prior bench work, but in the field they measure only PFAS, AOF and F⁻; CO₂ or carbon balances are absent.
claim_assessments.rationale: S07-E07/E07-E08 describe high-frequency ultrasound causing mineralization of PFAS via cavitation and cite prior bench work. S07-E01/E06 show that in the field study they measured PFAS, AOF, fluoride, TOC, COD, but there is no mention of CO₂ or explicit carbon mass balance. The lack of CO₂ data is inferred from the excerpts, not explicitly stated, so the negative part is only partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: AFFF and industrial matrices contain many more PFAS than appear in typical 12‑, 24‑, 28‑ or 40‑analyte panels; this is explicit in SCWO, HALT, MCD, HALT pilot, EO, and ultrasonication studies.
claim_assessments.rationale: S17-E02 notes that targeted analysis quantified only 28 PFAS while dozens of additional PFAS/organofluorines likely exist in AFFF. S13-E04/E05 state that theoretical total fluorine based on 40 analytes underestimates true fluorine, implying additional PFAS. S08-E03 says other PFASs were almost certainly present but not quantified. S05-E07 and E05 highlight ultrashort PFAS dominance and analytical limitations. S16-E05/E02 emphasize that most EO work uses narrow targeted panels missing many TPs. S11-E02/E03 discuss unknown precursors and ultrashort PFAS not captured by standard methods. Together they support the general statement.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Significant portions of fluoride and organofluorine cannot be linked back to identified PFAS because TF or TOF is not measured (e.g., SCWO continuous‑mixture, many plasma and ultrasonic runs).
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E02 shows fluoride and PFAS concentrations vs temperature but does not include total organofluorine; unresolved fluorine is implied but not quantified. S04-E02/E06 discuss fluorine mass balance and note VOFs and intermediates; full TOF is not measured. S11-E03/E07 describe incomplete mass balance due to missing ultrashort PFAS and unknown precursors. S14-E02/E05 describe fluorine tracking for parent/TP/F⁻ but acknowledge low recovery into quantified TPs. The overall claim that unresolved fluorine remains due to missing TF/TOF is consistent but partially inferential for some systems.

claim_assessments.claim_text: BN‑ball milling shows an 'incubation period' where PFAS loss precedes sharp F⁻ release; the incubation period lengthens as AFFF volume increases.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E08 reports an 'incubation period' before significant defluorination (DeF>50%), with destruction and F⁻ yield accelerating after 4 h for 100 µL and 6 h for 200 µL AFFF, and notes a positive correlation between AFFF load and incubation period.

claim_assessments.claim_text: GAP plasma shows PFOA destruction proceeding faster than defluorination.
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E05 notes that percent destruction decreases rapidly over time while defluorination progresses much more slowly due to C–F bond strength; S14-E08 shows 21% destruction vs 17% defluorination at 20 min, indicating faster parent loss.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Ultrasonication: PFOA/PFOS/6:2 FTS degradation efficiencies exceed defluorination across matrices.
claim_assessments.rationale: S11-E05 explicitly states that degradation percentages for PFOA, PFOS, and 6:2 FTS are higher than defluorination because many intermediates still contain fluorine. S11-E08 gives numerical examples with high degradation and lower defluorination.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In SCWO, defluorination lags DRE at intermediate temperatures.
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E03 notes that at 610–650 °C defluorination is not complete even when DRE is high; S03-E02 shows fluoride increasing with temperature while DRE is already high at 510 °C for PFCAs. S04-E08/E02 discuss differences between PFAS destruction and defluorination vs temperature. S02-E04 shows fluorine mass balance lagging at lower T. Together they support the statement.

claim_assessments.claim_text: IC LOD for F⁻ in ball‑milling and SCWO work is ~50 µg/L; FSE low‑spike MDL is ~0.2 mg/L.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E03 reports IC F⁻ detection limit 50 µg/L for AFFF BM work. S13-E03/E04 and S13-R03 reference IC with the same 50 µg/L limit via S01 methodology; SCWO IC LOD is not explicitly given in S17, but the claim only needs ball-milling and SCWO 'work', and at least BM is documented. S12-E03 describes low F− matrix spike 0.2 mg/L based on suggested FSE MDL, supporting 0.2 mg/L.

claim_assessments.claim_text: SCWO single‑compound and mixture studies use LC‑MS/MS LODs down to 0.05 ppb, LOQs 0.01–0.1 µg/L, and target 24–40 analytes.
claim_assessments.rationale: S04-E02 notes LC‑MS/MS LOD 0.05 ppb for PFAS and LOQ 0.01–0.1 µg/L. S14-E07 (though plasma, not SCWO) also reports LOQs 0.01–0.1 µg/L. S03-E08 notes 24 PFAS targeted. S13-E03 mentions 40 analytes in HALT, not SCWO; for SCWO, S02-E07 lists targeted sulfonates and PFCAs but not count. The LOD/LOQ figures and typical target list sizes are supported for SCWO via S04 and S03.

claim_assessments.claim_text: 'PFOA not detected' or 'PFAS below MDL' cannot be conflated with destruction, particularly when product suites and fluorine/TOC balances are incomplete.
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E08 discusses PFHxS being present below MDL in stock and detected in effluent, showing 'not detected' does not mean absent. S11-E02/E03 emphasize analytical challenges and unseen ultrashort PFAS, leading to incomplete mass balance despite disappearance of parents. S12-E02 warns that F− increases do not equal complete mineralization. Together they support the caution.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Batch PFOS SCWO gases were not analyzed; poor fluorine mass balance at 425–450 °C is attributed to lower MW fluorinated species in gas and/or liquid phases.
claim_assessments.rationale: S02-E08 states that gaseous products are not analyzed and that poor fluorine mass balance at 425 and 450 °C is attributed to potential formation of lower MW reaction products in gaseous and/or liquid phases.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Field‑scale SCWO and Krause’s AFFF demos note that small volatile organofluorines and smaller PFCAs are known possible byproducts but are not comprehensively quantified in each demo.
claim_assessments.rationale: S09-E07 and S17-E08 mention that SCWO stepwise destruction can produce small volatile organofluorines (e.g., trifluoromethane) and smaller PFCAs; S17-E08 notes these byproducts and that the time-limited demonstrations did not allow full byproduct assessment. However, 'not comprehensively quantified in each demo' is an inference about analytical scope; the excerpts do not tabulate byproducts at each site. Thus partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Plasma, ultrasonication and photodegradation create particulate or polymerized products requiring filtration before LC analysis, implying some fluorine resides in non‑dissolved fractions that are rarely characterized.
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E03 notes samples were filtered through 0.22 µm PES filters to remove polymerized products and particles before LC. S15-E03/S15-E05 state samples are filtered (0.22 µm) before analysis. S11 also mentions filtration for some analyses. The inference that these particulate fractions contain fluorine and are 'rarely characterized' is plausible but not directly demonstrated in the excerpts. Thus partial support.

claim_assessments.claim_text: EO with BDD anodes on landfill leachate shows broad transformation to many novel PFAS and other halogenated products but no fluorine mass balance.
claim_assessments.rationale: S16-E01/E04/E08 describe EO with BDD anodes generating numerous PFAS classes and halogenated TPs; S16 explicitly focuses on suspect/non-target screening with no mention of fluoride or fluorine mass balance in the excerpts, consistent with 'no fluorine mass balance'.

claim_assessments.claim_text: SCWO and HALT are currently the most advanced for combining parent loss, defluorination, and in some cases COD/TOC reduction, particularly for concentrated wastes such as AFFF and industrial brines.
claim_assessments.rationale: The cited SCWO (S02-S04,S09,S17) and HALT (S13,S05) studies indeed report high DRE, substantial defluorination, and COD or TOC reduction for concentrated PFAS streams (AFFF, industrial concentrates). The comparative statement that these are 'currently the most advanced' is evaluative and not source-based, but the underlying descriptive aspects are supported. Hence partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Field‑scale SCWO still leaves 20–30% of fluorine unresolved, and shorter-chain PFAAs/VOFs can appear as products.
claim_assessments.rationale: S09-E02 reports ~28.1% fluorine unrecovered in field-scale SCWO. S17-E02 shows large fractions of fluoride not explainable by targeted PFAS. S04-E06/E08 show PFCAs and VOFs (1H‑perfluoroalkane) as products in continuous SCWO. This supports the stated ranges and product formation.

claim_assessments.claim_text: HALT bench and pilot cases demonstrate high defluorination and near‑complete PFAS disappearance, but TOC and TP characterization are incomplete, especially for ultrashort PFAS.
claim_assessments.rationale: S13-E07/E08 show >99% PFAS loss and S13-E04 a fluoride yield >100% of theoretical, indicating near-complete defluorination at bench scale. S05-E03 defines defluorination and F mass recovery; S05-E02 indicates operating conditions chosen to 'ensure complete mineralization' but does not provide numeric DeF values in excerpts. S05-E02/E07 mention ultrashort FCAs dominating feeds and analytical limitations. However, explicit quantitative defluorination results from the pilot are absent in the excerpts, so claiming 'high defluorination' at pilot scale is inferred. The statement about incomplete TOC/TP characterization, particularly for ultrashorts, is consistent with S05 limitations. Overall partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Ball milling/mechanochemistry can achieve near‑complete defluorination of AFFF and very high targeted PFAS destruction in solids and undiluted foams, but about half the TOC remains and scalability and carbon fate remain open questions.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E01/E02/E08 report near-complete AFFF defluorination (99.7%, >98%) and destruction of targeted PFAS at bench scale. S01-E07 notes ~50% TOC remaining, and limitations mention unextractable fluorinated species and lack of CO₂ data. S08-E04/E07 show 99.88–100% destruction efficiencies for various matrices without providing TOC or CO₂, so carbon fate and scale-up are indeed open. The evaluative phrasing is consistent with the evidence.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Plasma, ultrasound, photocatalysis, and hydrodynamic cavitation can achieve rapid parent PFAS loss but often show defluorination lag and persistent short-chain/intermediate PFAS; few studies close even a liquid-phase fluorine balance and TOC reductions are much smaller than parent loss.
claim_assessments.rationale: S14-E05/E08 show destruction faster than defluorination and qualitative intermediate formation in GAP. S11-E05/E08 document high parent loss with lower defluorination and short-chain intermediates. S06-E02/E05/E08 report 20% defluorination with nearly closed parent+F− mass but no TP fluorine; the authors interpret near-mineralization but acknowledge lack of direct CO₂ data. S15-E06 shows 93% and 88% parent loss with only 27.1% and 23% TOC removal and 2.35% F recovery. None of these fully close fluorine and carbon balances; the statement is therefore supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: Proof-of-concept EC in DDW is a cautionary example: near‑quantitative parent removal with zero F⁻ indicates pure separation rather than destruction under these conditions.
claim_assessments.rationale: S10-E04 shows ~95–98% PFAS removal in DDW with no fluoride detected; S10-E08 states chemically inert PFAS were removed via electrocoagulation. This supports the interpretation that removal is by separation, not destruction.

claim_assessments.claim_text: BN‑ball milling: defluorination shows an 'incubation period' before a sharp increase; PFAS loss precedes F⁻ release.
claim_assessments.rationale: S01-E08 states that an incubation period precedes significant defluorination (DeF>50%) and that destruction and F− yield accelerate after certain times, with longer incubation at higher loads; S01-E01 shows early PFAS destruction and later defluorination. This supports the statement.

claim_assessments.claim_text: At 510 °C in continuous SCWO mixture, some PFSA species (PFOS and PFHpS) remain in the liquid effluent with DRE <40%, indicating residual parent PFAS despite complete loss of PFCAs below detection limits.
claim_assessments.rationale: S03-E03 notes that at 510 °C all PFCAs were below MDL while PFOS and PFHpS had DRE <40%. This matches the claim.

claim_assessments.claim_text: SCWO and GAP studies do not report direct measurements of CO₂ or other carbon-species balances, so mineralization and carbon fate cannot be fully assessed from their endpoints.
claim_assessments.rationale: None of the provided excerpts from S02–S04 or S14 mention CO₂ or inorganic carbon measurements; endpoints focus on PFAS, fluoride, and sometimes COD/TOC. However, the absence of such data in the excerpts is not explicit evidence that no such measurements exist anywhere in the papers, so the negative assertion is somewhat inferred. Partially supported.

claim_assessments.claim_text: In the Aquarden SCWO demo, fluorine in 28 targeted PFAS drops from 2.78 mg/L to 0.006 mg/L while fluoride rises from 26.0 to 97.5 mg/L, showing that targeted PFAS account for only 27% of effluent F⁻ and implying substantial defluorination of non-target organofluorines.
claim_assessments.rationale: S17-E06 presents these exact numbers and S17-E02 computes that only 25.9 mg F/L from targeted PFAS corresponds to 27% of measured 97.5 mg/L, leading authors to state that a large fraction of fluorine is not in the 28 targeted PFAS. This supports the interpretation.

claim_assessments.claim_text: None of the retained studies close both fluorine and carbon mass balances sufficiently to claim complete mineralization of a complex PFAS mixture.
claim_assessments.rationale: Across the provided excerpts, SCWO, HALT, plasma, ultrasound, HC, photocatalysis, EO, and MCD studies measure subsets of PFAS, fluoride, TOF/EOF, COD/TOC, etc., but none report both near-closed fluorine balances including all phases and full carbon balances including CO₂. However, the claim is a cross-study synthesis; while consistent with the evidence, it also asserts a universal negative that is not explicitly stated in any one source. Partially supported on that basis.
